title: Nakaʼela language - Wikipedia
text: Naka'ela. Nakaʼela is a possibly extinct Austronesian language spoken in Seram, Indonesia. Usage decreased after speakers moved out of the mountains.

title: Język naka’ela – Wikipedia, wolna encyklopedia
text: Język naka’ela – język austronezyjski z wyspy Seram w prowincji Moluki w Indonezji[1]. Posługiwali się nim mieszkańcy wsi Tanawa, Naka’ela i Hatu. W 1978 r. był jeszcze używany przez kilka osób.

title: Small Island Big Song: The Sounds of Austronesian Music
text: Linking Austronesia through music. The first album of the Small Island Big Song project comprised 18 songs recorded by producer BaoBao Chen and her husband, Australian music producer Tim Cole, during visits to more than 100 musicians in 16 Austronesian countries over three years.
